# **Gaps — no SOP yet**

- **Member Onboarding**: no documented first-touch-to-first-class flow (induction safety, goal capture, coach assignment, expectation-setting)
- **Member Checklists/Check-ins**: no cadence for 30-day, 90-day, 6-month touchpoints to assess progress and flag churn risk
- **Churn & Pause Management**: no process for managing cancellations, pauses, or win-back sequences (critical for retention)
- **Referral Programme**: no ops backbone for tracking referrals, reward distribution, or incentive compliance
- **Coaching Development Roadmap**: no progression framework for coach advancement (certification, specialisms, compensation)
- **Class Quality Audit**: no systematic quality assurance or coach observation protocol
- **Member Data & GDPR**: no documented data handling, consent, retention, or subject access request process
- **Complaints & Incidents**: no escalation, investigation, or resolution SOP (reputational and legal risk)
- **Finance (membership billing, refunds, disputes)**: assume weak—no SOP for payment failures, billing disputes, reconciliation
- **Health & Safety Incident Response**: no documented protocol for injuries, near-misses, accident reporting, follow-up

# Service Menu Execution for The Forge

• **Audit what you're ACTUALLY selling right now** — Have each coach log their last 10 client interactions (what they sold, how they explained it, what price they quoted). You'll likely find inconsistency that's costing you money. Use this to reverse-engineer your real offerings before documenting fake ones.

• **Price anchor from member pain, not cost-plus** — Don't build your menu around what feels fair to charge. Interview 5-8 members asking "what would you pay extra for?" (1-on-1 form checks? Nutrition guidance? Accountability calls?). Price the menu items based on what solves their actual bottlenecks, not gym convention.

• **Create two separate, visual menus** — Coaches need a decision tree (if member X wants Y outcome, sell Z package). Members need a simple one-pager showing: Base membership cost → Add-on options with exact inclusions → ROI (e.g., "PT: £X/session = £Y/month, includes 12-week plan"). Laminate it. Put it where people sign up.

• **Test before you "finalize"** — Roll out the new menu to 3 coaches first. Have them use it for 2 weeks, track which packages sell and which questions members ask most. Adjust based on real friction, then roll out firm version. This takes 3 weeks, not 3 months.

• **Assign ONE person (probably you) as "menu keeper"** — Every price change, new service, or coaching request gets funneled through one person. Prevents menu drift and keeps your income model from becoming chaos again in 6 months.

Audit class attendance by member tier (unlimited vs 4/8 class) and upsell idle unlimited members into nutrition coaching, PT bundles, or merchandise at £25–50/head. Target: recover to £130+/member by December.
